problem:
The center of the hyperbola $\frac{(y-7)^{2}}{25}-\frac{(x+11)^{2}}{49}=1$ is$\,\,($
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}
$).$
worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

Note that the given equation can be rewritten as follows:

$$
\frac{(y-7)^{2}}{{5}^{2}}-\frac{(x-(-11))^{2}}{{7}^{2}}=1
$$

In this case, we have $h=-11$ and $k=7.$

Therefore, the center of the hyperbola is $(\,-11,7\,).$
